scope: Two narrow Android 10 Lynx Sandbox correctness windows for Octane's native-list product path: ordinary-list reachability at 1,000 and 10,000 rows on f814e7942, followed by a 100-row current-product lifecycle fixture on c3210a17c that exercises background events and state, main-thread refs and events, Element PAPI reads and writes, a main-to-background callback, physical-node recycling, keyed state re-entry, and stale-handler replacement. This is semantic acceptance evidence, not a repeated performance, fling-smoothness, memory/GC, cross-framework, low-end, no-JIT, or iOS result.

historicalObserverCorrection.classification: observer and transport failure; no performance result
historicalObserverCorrection.candidateFailureCause: DOM.performSearch for bench-list-cell admitted both the list-item class bench-list-cell and its descendant class bench-list-cell-body, so the observer could select a non-list-item and report an undefined item-key even when the real list-item carried row-N.

repair.selectionContract: localName must be list-item and bench-list-cell must be an exact class token; malformed exact cells still fail

mainThreadElementDefect.observedFailure: On a real Lynx runtime, main-thread:ref.current was the opaque Element PAPI handle, so MainThread.Element.setAttribute and setStyleProperty were not functions. JSDOM hid the defect because its raw Element already has setAttribute.
mainThreadElementDefect.repair: Host ref mounts now wrap only native element handles in a MainThread.Element-compatible adapter; ordinary ref-value updates remain unwrapped. The adapter implements attributes, styles, selectors, computed-style reads, UI-method invocation, animation controls, and microtask-coalesced Element PAPI flushing.
regressionCoverage: opaque handle adaptation and flush coalescing
attribute, style, selector, measurement, invoke, and animation operations
host-only wrapping versus ordinary ref updates
